Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: explaining | explain | which explain | it explains
explanation: The independent clause after and needs a finite main verb for its subject (the wax cylinders they recorded), and explain supplies it. A's participle explaining leaves that clause without a verb, so the second half of the sentence is a fragment; C hides the verb inside a relative clause, so nothing is ever asserted about the cylinders; D restates the subject as it before explains, producing a run-on.

question:
The middle-distance runner who had always struggled with sprint finishes ____ last lap of the 1,500-meter final by several seconds, and her clubmates qualified for the national meet as well.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was winning the | winning the | it won the | won the
explanation: The long subject (the middle-distance runner who had always struggled with sprint finishes) still needs its own finite main verb, and won the last lap of the 1,500-meter final supplies it. A's progressive was winning the describes an activity in progress, which cannot combine with the completed result by several seconds; B's participle winning leaves the first clause with no main verb, so the sentence is a fragment; C repeats the subject as it, a run-on.

question:
When the herbarium in Vancouver re-examined its matsutake specimens, collected between 1950 and 1965, ____ a second, previously undescribed species hidden among the old sheets.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the identification of | their identification of | researchers identified | researchers identifying
explanation: The opening when clause is dependent, so the sentence needs a main clause with its own subject and finite verb, which only 'researchers identified a second, previously undescribed species' provides. A and B substitute the noun identification, leaving the sentence with no verb at all (and their in B has no antecedent); D's participle identifying gives the main clause no finite verb.

question:
The Enigma messages intercepted at Bletchley Park were useless until the codebreakers recovered the daily ____ the machine's rotors could then be stepped forward to the correct position.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: settings, so that | settings, | settings that | settings
explanation: The last stretch states a purpose and must be subordinated with so that, giving one properly joined sentence. B leaves two independent clauses tied by nothing but a comma, a splice; C's bare that turns the stretch into a relative clause on settings, which the rest of the clause cannot complete; D drops all punctuation and runs the clauses together.

question:
The museum's collection of Victorian insect mounts, which includes more than four thousand specimens gathered in the 1890s, ____ available to researchers who apply in advance.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: remain | remains | are remaining | have remained
explanation: Subject-verb agreement across an interrupting phrase: the subject is the singular noun 'collection', not the plural object of the preposition 'of Victorian insect mounts', so the singular verb 'remains' is required. 'Remain', 'are remaining', and 'have remained' all agree instead with the nearer noun 'mounts'. The relative clause 'which includes' already signals that the head noun is singular.

question:
The protected bike lane on Ninth Street and the pedestrian mall beside it ____ twice each spring by city engineers who check drainage grates and signage.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: is inspected | gets inspected | are inspected | was inspected
explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' form a compound subject, which takes the plural verb 'are inspected'. 'Is inspected', 'gets inspected', and 'was inspected' are all singular and would agree with only one half of the pair. The plural agent in the following clause, 'engineers who check', confirms that both features are serviced together.

question:
Each of the acetate master tapes in the climate-controlled vault ____ once a year so that archivists can confirm that the coating has not begun to shed.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: is played back | are played back | were played back | have been played back
explanation: The subject is 'each', a singular pronoun, and the prepositional phrase 'of the acetate master tapes' never changes that, so the singular 'is played back' is correct. 'Are played back' and 'have been played back' mistakenly agree with the plural noun 'tapes'. 'Were played back' uses the past, but 'once a year' together with 'can confirm' describes a recurring practice still in force.

question:
Elena Marsh is one of the marine biologists who ____ their coral nursery designs in open-access journals so that nearby reefs can be replanted before the next warming season.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: has published | publishes | had published | have published
explanation: In the construction 'one of the plural nouns who...', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural noun 'biologists', so the verb must be plural: 'have published'. 'Has published' and 'publishes' wrongly agree with 'one' instead of with the antecedent of 'who'. 'Had published' is past perfect, which the sentence never anchors to an earlier past event.

question:
The programming board of the municipal orchestra ____ each January as a single body, and its decisions about guest conductors shape the following season in detail.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: meet | meets | are meeting | have met
explanation: A collective noun acting as one unit takes a singular verb, and the sentence says exactly that: the board convenes 'as a single body' and is then referred to by the singular possessive 'its'. 'Meet', 'are meeting', and 'have met' are plural forms that would picture the members as separate individuals. The interrupting phrase 'of the municipal orchestra' supplies no second subject.

question:
In 1911 the Swedish expedition that charted the western glaciers of Spitsbergen ____ more than two hundred glass-plate photographs of the calving fronts on the west coast.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: takes | has taken | took | had taken
explanation: The stated date line, 'In 1911', marks a finished event, so the simple past 'took' is required. 'Takes' shifts a completed voyage into the present, and 'has taken' presents it as still bearing on now, which conflicts with the specific past date. 'Had taken' is past perfect, but nothing in the sentence happens later in the past than the photographing.

question:
Nineteenth-century chemists correctly reported that mercury ____ with sulfur at room temperature, an observation that later made the mixture useful for trapping vapors in sealed tubes.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: reacts | reacted | has reacted | had reacted
explanation: A general scientific fact keeps the simple present even when the surrounding sentence narrates the past, so 'reacts' is right. 'Reacted' backshifts a timeless truth as though the chemistry itself had changed. 'Has reacted' implies the reaction only began at some point and holds from then until now. 'Had reacted' is past perfect, needing a later past event to precede, which never appears.

question:
The director of the radio astronomy observatory, as well as two postdoctoral fellows, ____ the weekly reduction pipeline that converts raw spectra into open-access catalogs.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: review | are reviewing | have reviewed | reviews
explanation: 'As well as' adds information but does not create a compound subject, so the verb agrees with the singular head noun 'director': 'reviews'. 'Review', 'are reviewing', and 'have reviewed' all take the plural from the nearer noun 'fellows' inside the added phrase. Only a conjunction like 'and' would join two subjects here.

question:
Neither the transcript of the council hearing nor the two appended letters ____ the claim that the market was relocated in a single hot afternoon.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: supports | support | is supporting | has supported
explanation: With 'neither ... nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the plural 'the two appended letters', so 'support' is correct. 'Supports', 'is supporting', and 'has supported' all agree with the farther subject 'transcript' instead. Because the claim rests on documentary evidence, it is the letters that would or would not support it.

question:
Since the survey began in 2019, the glacier monitoring team ____ the same shoreline transect every fortnight, and its records now document six seasons of erosion.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: walked | had walked | has walked | walks
explanation: An interval that starts in the past and continues to now, flagged by 'Since the survey began in 2019' and confirmed by 'now document', takes the present perfect 'has walked'. 'Walked' cuts the work off in the past, and 'had walked' places it before another past event that never appears. 'Walks' ignores 'since', leaving the 2019 starting point unattached.

question:
By the time the crew replanted the marsh in the spring of 2018, the winter storms ____ the buried culvert that had drained the upland field for decades.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: wash out | have washed out | washed out | had washed out
explanation: 'By the time' plus a past clause ('the crew replanted ... in 2018') sets a past reference point, and an action completed before that point takes the past perfect 'had washed out'. 'Washed out' puts the storms at or after the replanting, contradicting 'by the time'. 'Wash out' and 'have washed out' bring present-time verbs into a sentence whose timeline sits entirely in 2018.

question:
Urban economics, a field that students often mistake for a branch of general sociology, ____ heavily on observational data because controlled experiments there are rarely feasible.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: depends | depend | are depending | have depended
explanation: The subject is the name of a single discipline, 'Urban economics', which is singular despite its final -s, so the singular 'depends' is correct. 'Depend', 'are depending', and 'have depended' are plural forms pulled toward the attractor nouns 'students' and 'experiments'. The appositive 'a field that students often mistake for a branch of general sociology' restates the subject as singular.

question:
A Listener's Guide to Birdsong, a field manual that several universities assign in their introductory courses, ____ its material by season rather than by species.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: arrange | arranges | are arranged | have arranged
explanation: A title naming one work is a singular subject, so the guide 'arranges' its material. 'Arrange', 'are arranged', and 'have arranged' all agree with the plural attractors 'universities' and 'courses'. The singular possessive 'its material' in the sentence confirms that the subject is the single volume.

question:
Curated for decades as a private cabinet of curiosities and kept in one locked room, ____ displayed to the public in the university's new exhibition hall this spring.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: many visitors watched the case be | the catalog of the collection was | the entomology collection is now | curators preparing the case had it
explanation: A participial phrase opening the sentence must modify the grammatical subject, and the only thing that was curated and locked away is the collection, so 'the entomology collection is now' attaches the modifier correctly. 'Many visitors watched the case be' and 'curators preparing the case had it' leave the modifier describing people who were never curated. 'The catalog of the collection was' attaches it to the catalog rather than to the objects themselves.

question:
To record the layout of the block before demolition began, ____ the interiors of all six ground-floor shops on medium-format film over two weekends in March.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: a photographic survey covered | the crew photographed | the interiors were photographed, documenting | documentation of the block required
explanation: An infinitive of purpose implies an agent with intentions, so the subject must be the people who did the recording: 'the crew photographed'. 'A photographic survey covered' and 'documentation of the block required' give the modifier an abstract subject that cannot set out to record anything. 'The interiors were photographed, documenting' makes the rooms, the things being photographed, the doers of the documenting.

question:
The heritage council argued with the housing developers for months, and in November ____ signed the agreement to widen the access road that had flooded every winter.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: they | whom | it | the developers
explanation: Two plural nouns, 'council' and 'developers', compete as antecedents, so a pronoun cannot say which party conceded; naming 'the developers' makes the reference exact. 'They' is the ambiguous pronoun whose nearest antecedent could be read either way. 'Whom' is an object form and cannot serve as the subject of 'signed', and 'it' has no singular antecedent that could sign anything.

question:
The illustrated field guide explains how to identify each warbler by its song, ____, and where the birds nest along the Pacific coast during the spring migration.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: when they arrive at the coastal marshes | the timing of their spring arrival | arriving in the coastal marshes in spring | the spring arrival of the birds is noted
explanation: The series is built from embedded questions introduced by interrogative words, 'how to identify...' and 'where the birds nest...', so the middle member must match: 'when they arrive at the coastal marshes'. 'The timing of their spring arrival' substitutes a noun phrase for a clause. 'Arriving in the coastal marshes in spring' inserts a participial phrase. 'The spring arrival of the birds is noted' is an independent clause, which breaks the embedded-question pattern.

question:
While restoring the seven-meter altarpiece, the conservator not only stabilized the flaking gesso on the central panel but also ____ before the visitors' gallery reopened in October.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the gold leaf at the edges was reattached | reattaching the loose gold leaf at the edges | reattached the loose gold leaf at the edges | reattachment of the gold leaf at the edges
explanation: 'Not only ... but also' demands parallel verbs, and the first member is the past-tense 'stabilized', so 'reattached the loose gold leaf' matches it. 'The gold leaf at the edges was reattached' switches to a passive clause with a new subject. 'Reattaching the loose gold leaf at the edges' leaves the second member without a finite verb, and 'reattachment of the gold leaf at the edges' replaces the verb with a noun.

question:
Unlike the hand-colored depth soundings that cartographers drew on eighteenth-century charts, ____ by satellite altimetry, which records subtle changes in sea-surface height above submerged ridges and seamounts.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: oceanographers obtain seafloor maps | modern seafloor maps are obtained | the technique of mapping the seafloor has been refined | measuring the seafloor is now done
explanation: 'Unlike' compares two like things, and what is being compared is eighteenth-century soundings, so the second term must be 'modern seafloor maps are obtained'. 'Oceanographers obtain seafloor maps' compares old charts to people, and 'measuring the seafloor is now done' compares them to an activity. 'The technique of mapping the seafloor has been refined' compares charts to a technique and leaves the sentence praising a method instead of a product.

question:
The archaeological society published ____ annual report three weeks early, along with the site drawings that two of the interns had finished over the summer.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: their | it's | whose | its
explanation: The antecedent is the singular collective noun 'society', which issues one report as one body, so the possessive pronoun 'its' agrees with it. 'Their' treats the society as a plural crowd of individuals. 'It's' is the contraction for 'it is', not a possessive, and 'whose' turns the clause into a relative clause that leaves the sentence with no main verb.

question:
Having surveyed the same shallow reef flat off the islands for six consecutive seasons, ____ thirty sponge colonies during the 2024 fieldwork, and the regional biodiversity register now cites those records.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the divers catalogued | thirty sponge colonies were catalogued by | the cataloguing of thirty sponge colonies was | colonies that the divers catalogued were
explanation: A perfect participial phrase at the start must attach to the doer of the surveying, which can only be 'the divers catalogued'. 'Thirty sponge colonies were catalogued by' makes the colonies the things that had spent six seasons surveying. 'The cataloguing of thirty sponge colonies was' gives an abstract action as subject, and 'colonies that the divers catalogued were' both dangles the modifier and leaves the clause without a completed verb phrase.

question:
Rangers for the coastal trust are responsible for maintaining the clifftop footpaths, monitoring erosion after heavy storms, and ____ the weathered timber boardwalks before the winter visitor season begins.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: to repair | repair of | replacing | being the repair of
explanation: The three duties follow the preposition 'for' and are built as gerund phrases, 'maintaining' and 'monitoring', so the third must be the gerund 'replacing'. 'To repair' switches to an infinitive, and 'repair of' drops in a bare noun with no verb sense and an ungrammatical following object. 'Being the repair of' stacks a clumsy passive gerund that does not match the active pattern of the list.

question:
At the harbor museum, ____ of the 1923 transatlantic flight were displayed beside the mechanic's original toolbag for a single week before the gallery closed for refitting.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: docents who explained the logbooks | logbook pages and spare propeller blades | the staff exhibited logbook pages | a catalog entry describing the aircraft
explanation: The introductory phrase 'At the harbor museum' sets a location, and the subject that follows should be the thing found on display there, which 'logbook pages and spare propeller blades' supplies. 'Docents who explained the logbooks' and 'the staff exhibited logbook pages' put people in the subject slot for a verb about exhibits. 'A catalog entry describing the aircraft' is only a noun phrase, so the sentence has no verb until its very end.

question:
The engineers sealed the joint where the concrete deck met the steel girder, but ____ continued to admit water after two further attempts in the same season.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: it | they | the deck | the joint
explanation: The sentence needs the leak path named outright, and only 'the joint' can sensibly admit water, so the explicit noun fixes the reference. 'It' is the trap: its nearest singular antecedent is 'the steel girder', the wrong noun. 'They' would point back to 'the engineers', who are the sealers rather than the leaking structure, and 'the deck' names a surface that the sentence has not described as the entry point for water.

question:
The revised catalog lists both the 1897 watercolors of the quarry and ____ , which lets visitors trace the artist's slow move from paint to printmaking.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the 1901 etchings | the etchings were printed in 1901 | printing the etchings in 1901 | the printer who produced the 1901 etchings
explanation: 'Both ... and' joins two items of one kind, and the first is the dated noun phrase 'the 1897 watercolors of the quarry', so the second must be the matching 'the 1901 etchings'. 'The etchings were printed in 1901' inserts a whole clause where a noun belongs. 'Printing the etchings in 1901' substitutes an activity for a group of objects. 'The printer who produced the 1901 etchings' parallels a person with a set of works.
